ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all proposed directors, ultimate beneficial owners, and senior management against the South African domestic sanctions and terrorism financing list under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act, United Nations Security Council Consolidated Listing, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, and UK HM Treasury sanctions list; enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons (PEPs), including family members and close associates, in accordance with FIC Directive 5 and Guidance Note 7; screening must be completed before incorporation, refreshed at least every 12 months, and repeated upon any trigger event, event of adverse media, or change of ownership.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC eServices (Companies and Intellectual Property Commission online corporate registry at www.cipc.co.za)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be submitted in any of the 11 official South African languages but must be expressed or transliterated into Latin alphabetic characters for CIPC processing; the name must include the legal suffix 'Proprietary Limited' or the abbreviation '(Pty) Ltd'; it must not be false, misleading, offensive, or contravene public policy, and must not falsely suggest a connection with the government, a municipality, a university, a statutory body, or a regulated profession.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, CIPC issues a written notice with grounds for refusal; the applicant may file an application for reconsideration with the Companies Tribunal in terms of section 160 read with regulation 9 of the Companies Regulations, 2011, using the prescribed adjudication form and paying the tribunal fee; alternatively, an applicant may bring an administrative-review application in the High Court under the Promotion of Administrative Justice Act 3 of 2000 within 180 days of the written refusal notice; both routes must attach the CIPC rejection reference, the proposed name and alternative names, legal argument demonstrating distinctiveness and non-conflict, and any prior document or trademark evidence.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are accepted by CIPC only if the registered office is a physical South African address with a street address that is accessible during ordinary business hours for service of formal legal notices; a virtual office cannot, by itself, satisfy the commercial-substance requirements for the ISIC 4220 municipal sewage treatment plant business, because the licence under the Water Services Act, environmental authorisation under NEMA, and municipal tender compliance require a substantive project office, engineering records storage, and site-control capacity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: CIPC does not routinely conduct unannounced inspections of private companies; however, unannounced on-site verification risk for this specific municipal sewage treatment EPC is quantified at approximately 35% within the first operating year due to Department of Water and Sanitation licence audits, National Treasury infrastructure-procurement reviews, and environmental-authorisation compliance site inspections.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended – sections 13, 14, 19, 40, 66, and 70
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), an agency of the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum authorized or paid-up share capital is prescribed. Shares may be issued for consideration permissible under section 40, and consideration must be received in full before allotment. No escrow account is mandated at incorporation; subscription funds are typically placed in a dedicated South African bank account pending allotment.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) the subscribers hereby subscribe for the initial issued share capital as set out in the subscription schedule, and such shares are allotted and issued in accordance with section 40 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008; (2) the registered office of the company be and is hereby established at [address], as stated in the Notice of Incorporation; (3) [Name] and [Name] are appointed as directors, and [Name] as Company Secretary; (4) the directors are authorised to open bank accounts, engage SARS, and execute all ancillary documents to give effect to these resolutions; (5) the accounting firm of [firm] is appointed as independent accounting officer.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reservation of Company Name and Pre-registration Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search on the CIPC database and submit an online name reservation application (Form CoR 9.1). The reserved name is protected for 20 business days and may be extended once for a further 20 business days. Incorporate the proposed name into the MOI before expiry to secure priority.
required_dossiers: Certified copies of directors' identity documents
Notarized power of attorney, if lodging through an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as confusingly similar to an existing name, file an application to the CIPC Name Tribunal or promptly reserve an alternative distinctive name within the remaining reservation window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of MOI and Notice of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Directors/Incorporators and Legal Advisors, CIPC for prescribed forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI) containing the company name, registered address, share classes, director powers, and governance rules; the MOI must not conflict with the Companies Act. Each incorporator must sign the MOI and complete Form CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation), including the registered office address and initial directors' details. The forms are then validated by a notary or commissioner of oaths where applicable.
required_dossiers: Consent to act by each initial director
Certified copies of identity documents of all incorporators and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CIPC flags a defective MOI or CoR 14.1, amend the documents and re-file via the same docket number within the statutory 20-business-day correction period to prevent abandonment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing and Payment of Incorporation Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC Customer Registration and Filing Centre (online via e-Services or servicedesk)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the customer entity on CIPC e-Services, upload the executed CoR 14.1 and MOI, and pay the prescribed filing fee (approximately ZAR 175, equivalent to about USD 10) by electronic funds transfer or card. CIPC will issue an acknowledgement of receipt and commence the statutory examination.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of CIPC filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC issues a notice of non-compliance for missing documents or incomplete fields, the applicant has 20 business days from notification to correct and resubmit; failure to remedy results in cancellation, requiring a fresh application with a new fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of Registration Certificate and SARS Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC; South African Revenue Service (SARS) via eFiling Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval CIPC issues the Certificate of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.3), recognizing the company as a separate legal entity. The company must then enroll with SARS within 60 days using the Registration, Amendments and Verification (RAV) form to obtain an income tax reference number, value-added tax (VAT) registration, PAYE, Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF) and Skills Development Levy (SDL) accounts.
required_dossiers: Identity documents and contact details of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS queries the registration, resolve the matter by submitting original certified documents and directors' affidavits to the local SARS branch or via eFiling correspondence, and apply for a correction of the tax registration within 30 business days; any tax registration penalty can be objected to under the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company's Board of Directors and appointed Company Secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting to formally adopt the pro-forma first board resolution, approve the share subscription and allotment, confirm the registered office, appoint officers, and approve the appointment of a registered accountant or accounting officer. Sign the minutes and the share register, and update the company's statutory records at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the First Board Meeting
Consent forms of the appointed accounting officer/auditor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a shareholder or director disputes the resolution, reconvene the board and pass a confirming resolution with revised quorum and notice requirements in accordance with section 70 of the Companies Act; any defective allotment can be ratified by special resolution.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Water and Sanitation (DWS) – Water Use Licensing Branch; Construction Industry Development Board (CIDB) for contractor registration and grading
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Water Use Licence under section 21 of the National Water Act 36 of 1998 and Effluent Discharge Permit; CIDB contractor grading certificate for design-and-commissioning EPC works

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE), acting with the relevant Provincial Environmental Authority
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 2 – Full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Report required for facilities or infrastructure for the treatment of effluent, wastewater, or sewage with a daily throughput capacity exceeding 2,000 cubic metres (GN 325, Listing Notice 2, Activity 4); Category 3 – Basic Assessment for smaller works below that threshold; municipal sewage treatment works in sensitive catchments are always subject to scoping and full specialist studies
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with DWS General and Special Standards under Government Notice 765/768 of 2018: treated effluent pH 5.5-9.5, BOD not exceeding 25 mg/ℓ, COD not exceeding 75 mg/ℓ, total suspended solids not exceeding 25 mg/ℓ, ammonia nitrogen not exceeding 6 mg/ℓ; potable-quality RO permeate must additionally meet SANS 241 drinking water specifications; VOC and chemical storage handling must follow the Waste Act norms and occupational exposure limits under the OHSA Hazardous Chemical Agents regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification per the National Building Regulations (SANS 10400 Part T) issued by the local municipality; structural load inspection certificate signed by an approved professional engineer; workplace clearance and occupational health compliance certificate issued by a certified health and safety agent under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993, verified by the Department of Employment and Labour.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); official portal: www.sars.gov.za; electronic filing via SARS eFiling (www.sarsefiling.co.za); company registry is the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A newly incorporated (Pty) Ltd must first be incorporated with the CIPC. Within 21 business days of incorporation or commencement of business, the company must register for income tax via SARS eFiling or a SARS branch using the 'IT/ PR for Companies' registration form. A 10-digit Income Tax Reference Number is issued. Where taxable supplies exceed or are reasonably expected to exceed ZAR 1,000,000 in any 12-month period, a VAT registration application (Form VAT 101) is compulsory; voluntary registration is permitted under a ZAR 50,000 threshold for non-resident suppliers of electronic services. For a non-resident-owned entity, the SARS registration file must be supported by the signed Memorandum of Incorporation, CIPC registration certificate, beneficial ownership declaration (CIPC Beneficial Ownership Register), bank confirmation of the South African bank account, and the SARS PIN/registration of each resident director. Non-resident directors must obtain a SARS taxpayer reference number and PIN. Registration must be maintained with annual filing of ITR14 income tax returns and VAT201 returns (monthly or two-monthly, at SARS discretion).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: A South African (Pty) Ltd is a resident company, taxed on worldwide income at the current corporate income tax rate of 27% for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023. The entity is not eligible for pass-through treatment; profits are taxed at company level and distributions are subject to dividend withholding tax at 15%. The permanent establishment and place-of-effective-management rules under the South African Income Tax Act No. 58 of 1962 apply to any non-resident parent or intercompany funding structures. Territorial scope: worldwide income accrues to the resident company, with foreign tax credits available under Part 2 of the Income Tax Act. No general tax-exempt-zone regime applies; municipal water treatment EPC income is fully taxable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa does not apply the US check-the-box system; an entity's classification follows the legal form under the Income Tax Act. However, relevant elections include: (i) section 11D research-and-development allowance election and pre-approval from the Department of Science and Innovation; (ii) accelerated capital allowances under sections 12B/12BA for renewable energy and water infrastructure assets; (iii) election to apply the hybrid-debt/equity re-characterisation rules in respect of back-to-back loans and hybrid instruments under sections 23M and 23N to align interest deductions with arm's-length substance; (iv) election for small business corporation (SBC) tax treatment under section 12E (applicable only if annual gross income does not exceed ZAR 20 million, not assumed for this EPC mandate); (v) election under the Taxation Laws Amendment Act for the place-of-effective-management concurrence with treaty residence, requiring notification to SARS of any dual-residency position.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the South African Value-Added Tax Act No. 89 of 1991, administered by SARS as a credit-invoice VAT system.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory VAT registration applies when actual or reasonable expected taxable supplies exceed ZAR 1,000,000 in any 12-month period (section 23(1), VAT Act). Non-resident suppliers of electronic services have a compulsory registration threshold of ZAR 50,000 per annum (section 54(2)(c)). A (Pty) Ltd engaged in EPC services is subject to the ZAR 1,000,000 threshold; municipal supply contracts typically exceed this, and registration is required from the date that the threshold is first exceeded, with VAT effective from the beginning of the month following registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping mandate is currently in force in South Africa. SARS has not activated a continuous transaction control (CTC) obligation; as of the 2024/2025 compliance cycle, there is no mandatory real-time validation of invoices through SARS. However, vendors must issue fully compliant tax invoices under section 20 of the VAT Act (vendor name, VAT number, invoice number, date, description, quantity, consideration exclusive/inclusive of VAT, and where applicable an abridged/application for credit note), and must retain them for at least 5 years. VAT201 returns and VAT201 declarations must be submitted electronically via eFiling; SARS may require payment of net VAT through the 'EasyPay' channel. SARS is testing a national e-invoicing interoperability framework; once gazetted, B2G supplies (including municipal infrastructure contracts) would be audit-trail critical, but no such mandate exists at the date of this dossier.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is claimable where a supply falls under section 11 of the VAT Act: (1) for goods – section 11(1)(a) applies to movable goods supplied to a non-resident recipient where the goods are exported from South Africa within 90 days of supply, and the supplier retains a signed declaration from the recipient of export, customs SAD500 export declaration and transport documents (Bill of Lading / air waybill); (2) for services – section 11(2)(k)/11(2)(l) applies where the services are physically rendered outside South Africa to a non-resident recipient for use wholly outside South Africa (e.g., offshore design, engineering and commissioning of a reverse osmosis municipal sewage treatment plant). Where the EPC contract is deemed to be performed partly in South Africa (engineering in SA, commissioning abroad), the zero-rating must be apportioned under section 11(2) read with SARS Guide VAT 404; all zero-rated supplies must be supported by export documentation retained by the supplier. Second-hand goods or goods made available to the exporter in South Africa are excluded from zero-rating if any input VAT was initially claimed and the goods are not physically exported.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500) lodged through a registered customs broker
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill evidencing physical export from South Africa
Commercial Invoice and export zero-rating statement (VAT 214 / VAT 214A) signed by the exporter and recipient
Foreign currency payment confirmation (SWIFT advice) or Inward Remittance Certificate issued by an authorised dealer (bank)
Proof of foreign export mandate / contract, including the signed EPC agreement with the non-resident municipal utility
SARS export clearance report (SAD list report) confirming export status
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS applies a risk-rating and audit programme to export zero-rating claims. Where the exporter fails to obtain or retain the mandatory export documentation bundle within the assessment period, SARS will disallow the zero-rating and assess output VAT at 15% on the export consideration (i.e., a full clawback of the VAT benefit). Additional VAT penalties apply under section 60 of the VAT Act (default penalty of 10% per month or part of a month, capped at 100%) and understatement penalties of 25% (standard), 50% (substantial understatement), 75% (gross non-disclosure), or 200% (intentional non-disclosure) under section 223 of the Tax Administration Act No. 28 of 2011. Fraudulent zero-rating claims, including false SAD500 declarations, fictitious exports or manipulated inward remittance certificates, attract criminal prosecution: SARS may impose a fine and imprisonment under section 234 of the Tax Administration Act and/or section 59 of the VAT Act; in addition, directors of the (Pty) Ltd are jointly and severally liable for debt arising from fraud where they knowingly participated. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within the 180-day deadline subjects the company to an Exchange Control penalty under the Currency and Exchanges Act No. 9 of 1933 and possible denial of tax clearance certificates; SARS may also disallow the corresponding input tax credits claimed on export-related expenses under sections 20(7) and 45 if the underlying export transaction is found to be fictitious. A retrospective VAT assessment may be raised within 5 years of the claim, and the completed plant assets, if returned into South Africa, would trigger an output VAT adjustment on fair market value.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) - Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), administering the Currency and Exchanges Act 9 of 1933, as amended, and the Exchange Control Regulations 2022 (GN No. 483 of 31 May 2022, effective 6 June 2022)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African Rand (ZAR) is fully convertible on the current account: authorised dealers (Tier-1 licensed commercial banks) may freely effect foreign-exchange conversions for genuine current-account payments such as imports, services, professional fees and interest, against a completed digital 'Form A' application and supporting commercial documentation, without SARB pre-approval for transactions up to the enhanced due-diligence threshold of ZAR 50 million per transaction. The capital account remains controlled rather than freely convertible: inward foreign direct investment (share subscription by non-resident shareholders) is permissible without SARB approval but must be routed through an authorised dealer and captured under the SARB Balance-of-Payments (BoP) statistical purpose codes for inward direct investment equity and inward intercompany loans. Profit remittance is achievable but documentary-burdened: a dividend to a non-resident shareholder requires (i) available distributable reserves evidenced by the latest audited annual financial statements; (ii) a board resolution declaring the dividend; (iii) completion of the SARB Form A with the non-resident shareholder declaration; and (iv) settlement through the authorised dealer, with Dividends Tax at the statutory 15% rate (or reduced treaty rate) withheld by the company. Repayment of shareholder loans and capital repatriation through share buy-backs are further conditioned on solvency and liquidity certification under the Companies Act 71 of 2008 and FinSurv reporting. There is no dual exchange rate and no material quantitative restriction on profit transfers once the documentary chain is complete, but every transfer exceeding ZAR 500,000 attracts a SARS tax-compliance-status screening by the authorised dealer.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Exchange Control Regulation 7 and the SARB Compliance and Surveillance Manual, export proceeds must be received in South Africa within 180 days of the date of export (90 days for certain perishable and agricultural goods) unless FinSurv has approved a longer period. The full contract or invoice value, representing effectively a 100% conversion mandate, must be routed to the exporter's authorised-dealer account, and the authorised dealer must convert the proceeds into Rand within 7 days of receipt (the surrender or realisation obligation), unless the exporter holds FinSurv approval to retain the foreign currency in an approved foreign-currency account for verified overseas liabilities. The exporter must close each transaction by delivering the finalised customs export declaration (SAD 500), bill of lading or airway bill, commercial invoice and proof of receipt or payment to the authorised dealer. Late receipt, under-receipt or non-receipt of export proceeds attracts administrative sanctions and potential criminal liability under the Currency and Exchanges Act. For a municipal water-treatment EPC contractor, the same regime applies to the export of plant, parts and technical services; services exports must be receipted within 180 days of completion of the service and likewise surrendered within 7 days of receipt.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Multi-Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-to-Medium for a South African resident operating entity. South Africa does not confer a passportable 'EMI' (Electronic Money Institution) authorisation on offshore digital money firms, and the National Payment System Act 78 of 1998, as amended, reserves the tier-1 settlement-account function to licensed authorised dealers (banks). A non-resident fintech or EMI must operate through a local banking-as-a-service partnership, act merely as an instruction channel, or use a registered Authorised Payment Provider (APSP) linked to a domestic settlement agent; it cannot open or maintain a South African domestic settlement account in its own name. The treasury blueprint therefore treats offshore EMIs (for example foreign currency e-wallets or international payment platforms) as non-settlement conduits only: the underlying ZAR clearing and foreign-exchange conversion must always be effected by a South African authorised dealer, and all exchange-control reporting (Form A, BoP capture, export surrender) remains the legal responsibility of the South African corporate and its domestic bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence requirement: High. The Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (FICA) requires the bank, as an accountable institution, to identify and verify every director, beneficial owner of 25% or more of the shareholding, and each authorised signatory. In practice, Tier-1 South African banks require at least two authorised directors or the mandated signatories to attend an in-branch FICA verification interview producing original passports, proof of residential address, the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) registration certificate, and the constitutional documents. Remote onboarding is available only in narrow cases: a director may be interviewed at a foreign branch or representative office of the same banking group, or may submit a banker's confirmation (reliance letter) issued by a FATF-compliant foreign bank acceptable to the local lender, together with notarised identity documents and locally executed CIPC appointment forms. Fully digital onboarding of a newly incorporated, non-resident-controlled (Pty) Ltd is not generally available under current FICA risk-based practice.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial ownership with 100% offshore control and no demonstrated local economic substance or trading history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full FICA beneficial-ownership declaration filed through the CIPC Beneficial Ownership Register under the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022; CIPC Certificate of Incorporation; shareholders register; notarised passports and tax residency certificates of all 25%+ shareholders; and a substance cover letter evidencing local management office, South African board meetings, local employment, and the municipal project award pipeline.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection originating from a FATF grey-listed or high-risk tax jurisdiction, or from a remitter not named as the subscriber or lender in the corporate transaction documents
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-funds and source-of-wealth statements covering six months of bank statements of the remitting entity; executed share subscription or shareholder loan agreement; intercompany transactional trail; legal opinion issued by a law firm in a FATF-compliant jurisdiction; and a completed bank enhanced due-diligence questionnaire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large project mobilisation or escrow payments received by an EPC contractor without a demonstrable underlying municipal or multilateral contract
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed municipal tender award notice or World Bank/DFI award letter; full EPC contract including commercial schedules; the underlying project financing agreement and escrow instruction letter; engineer's notice to proceed; and any statutory licences relevant to municipal sewage or reverse-osmosis works, such as a water-use licence issued by the Department of Water and Sanitation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value outward payments to an offshore plant or membrane supplier inconsistent with the company's stated trading profile and project stage
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed procurement agreement; supplier due-diligence file; SARB Form A application supported by supplier invoice and customs import entry (SAD 500); bill of lading or airway bill; evidence of project-stage milestone certification; and for letter-of-credit disbursements, the negotiating bank's presentation schedule and the issuing bank's LC record.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity subscription and shareholder loan proceeds must be remitted by SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 COVER for interbank cover) to the company's domestic account at a South African authorised dealer. The reference field must identify the issuer and the transaction, for example 'ZA_PTY_LTD - Share Subscription' or 'ZA_PTY_LTD - Shareholder Loan'. South Africa does not use IBAN: the remitter must use the bank BIC, the 9-digit branch code and the domestic account number. The authorised dealer captures the transaction under the SARB BoP recording framework: inward direct investment is logged under the direct-investment inward equity purpose codes, inward intercompany loans under the loan purpose codes, and escrow deposits from a multilateral development bank (notably a World Bank project account) under other inward transfers where the escrow is held by the project owner. Verification package: (i) certified board resolution approving the share issue or loan and appointing signatories; (ii) executed subscription agreement or loan agreement stating the interest rate, maturity and the SARB-required secondary-lending restriction for offshore loans; (iii) source-of-funds documentation for each wire; (iv) FICA entity file and beneficial-ownership records; (v) updated Companies Act securities register showing non-resident shareholders marked as 'Code NR'; and (vi) for escrow-funded mobilisation, the municipal project award letter and the escrow instruction letter.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements are executed through two primary clearing rails: SWIFT MT103 direct remittances for advance payments, certified progress payments and supplier invoices; and commercial documentary credits (sight or usance letters of credit) opened by SWIFT MT700 and negotiated against presentation of MT7xx-series conforming documents. All outward foreign-exchange conversions require the authorised dealer to process a digital Form A application supported by the purchase order, EPC contract schedule, supplier invoice and, where goods are imported, the SARS customs entry (SAD 500). Payments for current-account purposes up to ZAR 50 million per transaction do not require FinSurv pre-approval; amounts above that threshold, or payments involving unusual counterparty or geographic risk, trigger enhanced due diligence and a possible FinSurv referral. Payments to an offshore reverse-osmosis plant supplier under a municipal water-treatment contract are classified as payments for construction services and works, and the bank will require independent certification of the physical progress milestone by the client or engineer. For LC operations, the issuing South African bank requires an offshore funded balance, a cash cover, or an escrow assignment over the project proceeds as collateral for the LC facility.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward exchange contracts (FECs) - deliverable ZAR/USD, ZAR/EUR and ZAR/GBP forwards of up to 12 months concluded through a South African authorised dealer against documentary evidence of the underlying EPC trade or escrow-denominated exposure

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on ZAR executed with an authorised dealer or offshore bank where the reference currency pair requires offshore settlement, subject to the underlying commercial exposure being documented and non-speculative

Cross-currency swaps (CCIRS) to manage long-duration mismatches between USD-denominated World Bank escrow receipts and ZAR-denominated local construction costs, permitted with authorised-dealer approval and underlying project documentation
European-style currency options and range forwards purchased through an authorised dealer to protect tender-to-contract conversion risk on USD-denominated project escalation and mobilisation payments

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return (electronic filing; statutory fee tiered by declared annual turnover - representative mid-tier fee of ZAR 1,000 shown)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation (Companies Act 2008, s.33)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of approximately ZAR 500 (approx. USD 27) per annual return; non-filing for two consecutive years triggers CIPC deregistration (administrative strike-off) under s.82(7) after compliance notices and a cure window; directors personally liable for administrative penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Register (BOR) Annual Confirmation and Declaration - filed together with the CIPC Annual Return; no separate CIPC fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CIPC Beneficial Ownership Transparency Register (GLA Amendment Act 2022, s.56B)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 business days of the incorporation anniversary (with the annual return); event-driven re-filing within 5 business days of any shareholding transfer or change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CIPC compliance notice with escalating administrative fines; directors may incur personal liability for a false or incomplete BOR; repeated default supports deregistration action and referral to the Financial Intelligence Centre for AML/CFT enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: SARS Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (ITR14) - final normal tax return, together with supporting AFS and tax computations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 12 months after the end of the financial year; provisional tax estimates (IRP6) payable at the 6-month and 12-month marks of the year of assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% non-compliance penalty on assessed tax plus interest at the prescribed SARS rate; fixed monthly administrative penalties up to ZAR 2,500 (approx. USD 135) per month for persistent non-submission; revocation of tax clearance status and exposure to criminal sanctions for wilful default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS) - preparation under IFRS/IFRS for SMEs, audit or independent review, and delivery to shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders in General Meeting (Companies Act s.30); approved AFS retained at the registered office for CIPC record-keeping inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AFS approved by the board and delivered to shareholders within 6 months after the financial year-end; filing with CIPC is not required for a private company unless it is public, state-owned, or the Commission so directs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CIPC compliance notice with administrative penalties on directors; restrictions on dividends and distributions until AFS are approved and delivered; directors personally liable for knowingly false or misleading financial statements.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit where the Public Interest Score (PIS) is 350 or more, or where the company is public or state-owned (Companies Act 2008, s.90 and Regulations 26-28). For PIS of 100-349, an audit is required unless an independent review is elected with shareholder approval and the Memorandum of Incorporation permits it. For PIS below 100, neither audit nor independent review is required unless the Memorandum of Incorporation prescribes it or shareholders holding at least 5% of voting rights request it.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB (fully adopted in South Africa); IFRS for SMEs available for entities without public accountability and with PIS below 350; no separate national GAAP remains in effect.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain a Beneficial Ownership Register (BOR) at its registered office and file it with CIPC under s.56B (inserted by the General Laws Amendment Act 2022). The annual return anniversary is the compulsory annual confirmation point: the directors must certify that the BOR is complete, true, and current. Any shareholding transfer must be recorded in the securities register and BOR immediately, with a CIPC re-filing within 5 business days of the change.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 200 - USD 800 per annum (registered office address plus CIPC filing and company-secretarial services; Johannesburg/Cape Town corporate service provider market range)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 - USD 12,000 per annum (independent audit for a mid-sized EPC / water-treatment private company; independent-review option materially lower)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holidays; dividends declared are subject to the South African Dividends Tax at 20%; the Section 12J Venture Capital Company regime has been terminated for new investments after 30 June 2021, but historical investors may still claim deductions over their 5-year holding period. Municipal sewage treatment EPC activities may qualify for the Section 12B accelerated capital allowance on movable assets used in water treatment infrastructure, and the Section 11D Research and Development deduction (up to 10% additional deduction for qualifying R&D) where applicable. South Africa applies a general corporate income tax rate of 27% for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 (Income Tax Return for Companies) filed via SARS eFiling; Companies must be registered for Income Tax and obtain an Income Tax Reference Number.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return and payment of normal tax are due within 12 months of the company's financial year-end, unless the company qualifies as a provisional taxpayer, in which case two provisional tax payments (six-month top-up and six-month final top-up) are due and the annual return due date is the same 12-month deadline. SARS estimates and assesses where a return is not filed; interest and penalties accrue automatically.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, trading name, postal and registered physical address, and SARS taxpayer reference number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a South African resident private company with non-resident shareholders, enter the South African registered details; non-resident shareholders do not file ITR14 unless they have a South African permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) registration number, incorporation date, and financial year-end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the South African CIPC number even if the ultimate parent is a non-resident; do not enter the foreign parent's registration number.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Local and foreign gross income; exempt income includes gross dividends received (subject to the dividends exemption) and certain foreign dividends if the participation exemption applies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies with a South African PE must report only South African source income attributable to the PE; foreign dividends are excluded where the South African participation exemption election is made.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate taxable income after deducting allowable expenditure, capital allowances, and claiming assessed losses brought forward (maximum five years).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident PE must claim deductions only if directly attributable to the PE; the branch remittance base is the taxable income attributable to the PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the 27% statutory rate to taxable income; rebates, prepayments, and provisional tax credits are then deducted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PE profits are also subject to the 27% rate; the branch rate is the same because South Africa does not levy a separate branch profits tax beyond the general corporate income tax and the dividends tax on branch distributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital gains tax inclusion rate of 80% of net capital gain plus Section 8 recoupments of capital allowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PE is subject to CGT only on immovable property in South Africa or assets effectively connected to the PE; specify PE disposal proceeds separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the two provisional tax payments made during the year plus any foreign tax credits, PAYE credits, and withholding tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies with a PE must make provisional payments using IRP6; foreign taxes on income attributable to the PE may qualify for rebate under Section 6quat if proved with a foreign tax certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 (Assessed Loss and Tax Loss Carryforward Schedule)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute the balance of assessed loss available after the current year, evidenced by an assessed loss ruling or previous ITR14.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident PE may carry forward an assessed loss incurred in South Africa; a change in ownership may trigger the loss restriction rules under Section 20(2A).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Although on the income tax return, indicate local business activity classification and whether the company is a registered VAT vendor; cross-check with VAT201 reconciliations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident EPC contractors performing construction in South Africa must register for VAT and complete VAT 201; the income tax return cross-references VAT information for audit matching purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare dividends paid and dividends tax withheld; the company acts as withholding agent for the 20% dividends tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where dividends are paid to a non-resident shareholder, dividends tax must be withheld at 20% unless a DTA reduction is evidenced by a declaration and undertaking from the shareholder; use the DTA declaration form (DTD) and withholding direction (DTW).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file an ITR14 on time attracts an automatic administrative penalty (up to 10% of assessed tax for non-provisional taxpayers, or 5% for provisional taxpayers), a monthly penalty of up to 1% of the outstanding tax for each month of default, and interest at the prescribed rate (currently approximately 10.5% per annum) on underpaid tax. Criminal non-compliance can result in imprisonment up to two years. SARS may also issue an estimated assessment enforceable immediately.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% Dividends Tax levied on dividends declared and paid by the South African company to shareholders, regardless of shareholder residence; no secondary tax on companies (STC) remains.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, a non-resident shareholder must complete and furnish SARS with (a) a Declaration by the Beneficial Owner of Dividends (DTD form) and (b) a Direction to withhold at reduced rate (DTW form) before the dividend is paid. For interest, royalties, and other considered payments, the non-resident recipient must submit a completed DTA declaration and undertaking (typically form IT10(a) or applicable SARS DTA relief forms), together with a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the treaty jurisdiction's competent authority, substantiating economic and beneficial ownership. SARS requires the TRC to specify the tax year and residency period; the payer must retain the documents for five years. Treaty relief is denied where a principal purpose of the arrangement is treaty shopping (PPT / limitation of benefits clauses in South African DTAs).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory 15% withholding tax on interest (SDI) paid to non-residents; treaty-reduced rates commonly 0% (e.g. many treaty partners with no source-state interest tax where recipient is beneficial owner), or 10%/5% under applicable DTAs. Royalties: statutory 15% withholding tax on royalties paid to non-residents; treaty-reduced rate under most South African DTAs is 10% (often 7.5% or 5% under specific treaties, but standard DTA rate is 10%; the South Africa-US treaty reduces to 0% for certain royalties). The DTA rate depends on the specific treaty and the beneficial owner. Technical service fees that are not royalties and not connected to a PE may not be subject to South African withholding tax unless the DTA deems them to be royalties or where the payer is a South African resident and the fee is for the use of intellectual property. The 15% domestic rate applies to royalties (including deemed royalties for the use of know-how), and the 15% domestic rate on interest is reduced to 0% under most current DTAs.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: In South African Rand (ZAR): (1) A full Local File and Master File are required where the covered transaction(s) exceed ZAR 100 million (aggregate cross-border connected-person transactions; for local transactions, ZAR 50 million per transaction or ZAR 100 million in aggregate). SARS also requires a CUP or other comparable benchmark documentation if the value exceeds ZAR 10 million for a single cross-border transaction, and a contemporaneous TP policy is mandatory where a connected person is involved and the transaction exceeds ZAR 5 million in total. SARS Practice Note 7 and the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines apply.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Africa applies the Economic Substance Requirements (ESR) under the OECD Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) framework only in so far as the substance is embedded in the transfer pricing and controlled foreign company (CFC) attribution rules under Section 31 and Section 9D of the Income Tax Act. There is no separate statutory 'Economic Substance Regulations' filing regime (such as Abu Dhabi or Cayman), but SARS may apply the General Anti-Avoidance Rules (GAAR) under Section 103 and Section 80A-L, and a shell company with no real economic substance is not recognised for treaty benefits. The CFC rules require South African resident shareholders holding more than 50% of the participation rights to include the attributable net income of a CFC unless the CFC has substantial economic substance (i.e. the CFC carries on real business activity, has premises, employees, equipment, and a substantive local management) and the income is not passive. For an EPC sewage treatment construction company, the entity must demonstrate real operational substance: local project management offices, engineering staff, hazardous-water treatment skilled personnel, equipment ownership, risk assumption, and board decision-making in South Africa. The SARS TP rules also require that no profit is shifted to low-tax jurisdictions unless the entity has the capability and actual performance of the functions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Tax Avoidance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting EPC contract revenue, submitting false VAT201 refunds for reverse osmosis equipment purchases, backdating invoices to shift profit to a connected foreign supplier, using a shell entity to receive contract proceeds, or fraudulently claiming the Section 12B allowance for assets not used in water treatment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Section 234 and 235 of the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011: a penalty of up to 100% of the evaded tax and an additional amount determined by SARS (up to 200% in aggravated cases), civil interest at the prescribed rate, and criminal liability with a fine of up to ZAR 10 million or imprisonment for up to ten years, or both. In flagrant cases, the Tax Administration Act allows criminal prosecution without prior assessment. SARS may also impose an understatement penalty under Section 222 ranging from 10% to 150% of the shortfall, depending on the behaviour; intentional tax evasion attracts a 150% understatement penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held jointly and severally liable for the company's tax debts under Section 179 of the Tax Administration Act if they knowingly fail to pay PAYE, VAT, or provisional taxes (a 'representative taxpayer' obligation). Fraudulent conduct pierces the corporate veil: directors face criminal imprisonment up to five years, travel bans enforced under the Administration of Estates Act and the Corruption Act, and disqualification from holding office where SARS proves any known participation in fraudulent evasion. Civil restitution for the full unpaid tax plus costs is enforceable personally.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Excessive Interest Deductions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting the EPC contract consideration with a connected offshore service provider at a non-arm's length margin (e.g. booking a 90% profit margin in an UAE or Mauritius services entity without staff), granting intra-group loans at inflated interest rates, failing to file the mandatory transactional net margin TNMM or CUP documentation once the ZAR 5 million / 10 million / 100 million thresholds are triggered, or making excessive interest payments that are not deductible due to the debt-to-equity thin capitalisation rules and Earnings Stripping Rules under Section 23N.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS has the power to adjust the taxable income under Section 31(2) of the Income Tax Act to reflect an arm's length price; a 150% understatement penalty for substantial understatement of tax due to intentional or gross-culpable TP mispricing applies; interest runs on the adjusted assessment from the original due date; the financial debt interest deduction may be denied or limited under Section 23N, and the GAAR under Section 80A-L can void the entire arrangement. A TP audit may lead to a reallocation of profit that also triggers the CFC attribution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false TP documentation or intentionally structure a transaction to avoid tax are personally liable to SARS under the de facto control or enabler provisions of the Tax Administration Act. Criminal sanctions include imprisonment up to 5 years for applying a tax avoidance arrangement that is 'highly artificial', and travel bans may be imposed pending finalisation of a criminal investigation. Civil claims for damages may also arise from shareholders or the State under the Prevention and Combat of Corrupt Activities Act where a bribe facilitated the mispricing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a South African (Pty) Ltd without a physical office, employees, or genuine board authority while invoicing municipal clients for reverse osmosis plant design and commissioning; routing all profits to a zero-tax jurisdiction without local substance; failing to hold the statutory Water Services Act licence and EIA approvals; using the shell solely to issue lease invoices and dividend payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS can disregard the corporate entity under the GAAR (Section 80A-L); beneficial ownership and substance analysis under DTA relief strips the shell of treaty benefits; the CFC rules can attribute undistributed income if the foreign entity is not bona fide resident; the shell may be struck from the CIPC register under the Companies Act 71 of 2008 for non-compliance, and SARS may raise a deemed assessment on the natural person controlling the shell. Administrative penalties under the Companies Regulations (ZAR 100 per day for failure to file annual returns) and the Tax Administration Act ZAR 1 million penalty for deliberate non-disclosure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who conceal a shell variety are jointly liable under Section 22 and Section 77 of the Companies Act for reckless trading, and they face a direct SARS claim for diverted profits under the statutory piercing provisions. Under the Protection of Constitutional Democracy Against Terrorist and Related Activities Act, failing to report unusual structured payments may be treated as a money laundering offence, carrying imprisonment up to 15 years. Directors may be subjected to asset freezes, travel bans, and extradition under mutual legal assistance treaties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Beneficial Ownership Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A low-risk sewage treatment EPC company nonetheless failing to file accurate beneficial ownership information with the CIPC, accepting a World Bank escrow or SWIFT wire from an unknown municipality or intermediary without applying FICA due diligence, failing to verify the ultimate beneficial owner of a non-resident shareholder, or making repeated dividends to tax-heaven shell accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (FICA), as amended by the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combatting Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 2022, imposes administrative fines for accountable institutions of up to ZAR 100 million per contravention; directors may be held liable. A failure to register beneficial ownership with CIPC (Companies Act 2008 section 50) results in a penalty up to ZAR 1.5 million; deliberate misleading statements expose the company to criminal penalties up to ZAR 10 million or ten years' imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who knowingly conducts a transaction using proceeds of tax evasion or who is negligent in identifying a shareholder's source of funds commits an offence under FICA sections 46 and 46A: imprisonment up to 15 years and a fine up to ZAR 100 million; the court may order restitution and grant a travel ban or confiscation order under the Prevention of Organised Crime Act 121 of 1998. Corporate veil piercing applies when the company is used as the instrumentality of money laundering, and the director can be sued for civil damages.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits via a 'loan' to a connected non-resident without withholding 20% dividends tax, striking artificial dividends paid by interposing a conduit entity, failing to obtain the DTD/DTW declaration and TRC, or paying dividends to a jurisdiction with which South Africa has no DTA without withholding the full 20%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The dividend withholding agent is assessed for 20% dividends tax plus a penalty of up to 10% for late payment and interest; under section 64Q of the Income Tax Act, the company remains liable to SARS for any unrecovered withholding; secondary liability attaches to the shareholder. The Tax Administration Act understatement penalty of 50% applies for failure to withhold by a company, and SARS may treat the repayment of the loan as a dividend in specie under section 64E, triggering full dividends tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign off dividend payments without ensuring the proper DTD/DTW forms and TRC are knowingly responsible for a SARS claim and may be prosecuted for a false declaration; imprisonment up to four years and personal payment of the unpaid dividends tax plus interest. If the court finds that the director used the company to strip profits to evade taxes, the court may be able to apply the Section 64Q deeming provision to hold the director personally liable for the dividends tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Late Filing / Estimated Assessments and Process Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Missing the 12-month ITR14 filing deadline, failing to pay the first provisional tax top-up, not responding to a SARS audit query on TP documentation, or refusing to submit water treatment project cost schedules after a SARS section 12B claim.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS automatically issues an estimated assessment; the filtering penalty is the greater of 5% (provisional) or 10% (non-provisional) of the outstanding tax, plus monthly 1% penalty and interest at 10.5% per annum. If the estimated assessment is fraudulent, the criminal offence of tax evasion with a fine up to ZAR 10 million and imprisonment up to 10 years applies. A taxpayer that fails to keep records for five years faces an additional penalty of up to ZAR 10 million under section 31 of the Tax Administration Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a provisional taxpayer that fails to pay provisional tax are jointly and severally liable for the provisional tax debt under section 14(5)(c) and section 179 of the Tax Administration Act, without the need for a criminal conviction. Where a director was responsible for the failure to file due to gross negligence, the court may grant SARS an attachment order and impose a travel ban; personal liability is not capped by the corporate limited liability status.
